dct_title_s: Nepal Flood 2026 Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River Corridor
dct_description_sm: OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps vector layers for the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridor in Bagmati and Gandaki Provinces, Nepal, extracted for the 2026 flash flood response. The area of interest is a 1 km buffer around the river centrelines, covering 314.30 square kilometres. It runs from Rasuwagadhi on the China border, down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli, to the Narayani confluence at Devghat in Chitwan. It crosses six districts, Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahu and Chitawan, and twenty municipalities. The corridor merges two sources: the original partner shapefile for the upper reach and OCHA's HPCS 1 km corridor for the downstream reach. A small part of the buffer above Rasuwagadhi falls inside China, where the OpenStreetMap country extract has no coverage. Every layer is published here as a resource, and most layers carry two versions, one from OpenStreetMap and one from Overture Maps. The two are not interchangeable: - **OpenStreetMap** layers are live. They are rebuilt daily from the latest OSM data, so they pick up work by volunteer mappers as the response progresses. Use these when currency matters. - **Overture Maps** layers fuse building footprints and other features from Microsoft, Google and OpenStreetMap. That fusion gives broader coverage than OSM alone in places volunteers have not reached yet, but **Overture is not updated daily**. It follows Overture's own release cycle, so it will not reflect mapping done during this response and will fall progressively further behind the OpenStreetMap layers. In short, Overture is wider but older; OpenStreetMap is current. For damage assessment against the latest mapping, prefer the OpenStreetMap layers and treat Overture as a supplement where OSM coverage is thin. Mapping task boundaries from the Tasking Manager campaign are published here too and refreshed daily, showing where volunteers are being asked to map. The bridge damage assessment is contributed by [ICIMOD](https://www.icimod.org/), the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development. - Source: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/), [ICIMOD](https://www.icimod.org/) - Part of HOT disaster response exports on HDX by [HOT](https://www.hotosm.org/)
